author: Sideprojects
description:
From sixteenth-century Mexico to twentieth-century Paraguay, missionaries burned sacred books, destroyed temples, ran courts with execution powers, and organised forced relocations of isolated peoples. This episode examines seven cases where spreading faith became inseparable from colonial violence, land seizure, child removal, and thousands of deaths caught between empires and belief.
